headline: COPPER TARIFF PLAN STALLS — WHITE HOUSE AFFORDABILITY FEARS SINK PLAN THAT DROVE METAL TO $14,703/T RECORD
snippet: Reuters reported September 10 that the White House copper tariff plan has stalled: administration sources say affordability concerns ahead of November's midterm elections are giving officials pause on the proposed 15% tariff on refined imports slated for January 2027, escalating to 30% in 2028. That tariff threat had driven traders to stockpile copper in US warehouses, pushing LME prices to an all-time high of $14,703/t — and copper fell sharply on the news as the premium built on those tariff expectations began to unwind.

headline: GOLD SURGES TO TWO-MONTH HIGH AT $4,444, THEN REVERSES SHARPLY — MIXED PPI DATA 'CAUSED BOTH MOVES'
snippet: Gold spiked to a two-month high near $4,444/oz Thursday morning before reversing sharply to $4,383 after August PPI printed +5.4% YoY — slightly above consensus — but with a softer-than-forecast core reading of +0.2% vs +0.3% expected. Friday's CPI is now the single decisive input before the September 16-17 FOMC: a hot headline could push rate-hike odds above 70% and send gold toward $4,300-$4,350 support, while a soft print could reopen a run at today's two-month high.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE SWAPS ALASKA VMS PROJECT FOR 22% STAKE IN VIZSLA COPPER — NO CASH CHANGES HANDS IN ASSET-FOR-EQUITY DEAL
snippet: Agnico Eagle (TSX/NYSE: AEM) announced September 8 that it will transfer the Delta polymetallic VMS project (historical inferred 15.4 Mt at 0.6% Cu, 3.8% Zn, 1.7 g/t Au, 62 g/t Ag) and Helm Bay gold project in Alaska to Vizsla Copper Corp. (TSXV: VCU) in return for approximately 22% of Vizsla's issued shares plus 3.04 million warrants at C$1.95, retaining a 2-3% NSR royalty on both properties. The all-equity structure — a tier-one miner recycling non-core exploration assets into meaningful junior copper equity — is an increasingly common template in a market where quality copper juniors trade at premiums.

headline: PROSPECTOR ML26-46: 24.2 G/T AU, 31.6 G/T AG AND 1.62% CU OVER 3.5M — YUKON TESS ZONE OPEN IN THREE DIRECTIONS
snippet: Prospector Metals Corp. (TSXV: PPP) released September 10 results from hole ML26-46 at the TESS gold-silver-copper discovery in Yukon: two high-grade intercepts including 24.2 g/t Au, 31.6 g/t Ag and 1.62% Cu over 3.5m at 67.6m depth, and 14.7 g/t Au, 47.7 g/t Ag and 1.81% Cu over 2.1m at 43.4m — the strongest individual intercepts yet at the discovery. The TESS Zone is now defined over at least 200m of strike and 150m of depth in a tabular 15-25m-wide northeast-trending structural corridor, open along trend and at depth, with 88 holes into the fully funded 25,000m program.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING (DSV) EARNS SPOT IN 2026 TSX30 WITH 934% THREE-YEAR GAIN — BORDEN AND PORCUPINE DEALS PAY OFF
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX: DSV) was named to the 2026 TSX30™ on September 9 with a 934% dividend-adjusted three-year return — generating approximately $6.6 billion in market cap growth as of June 30, 2026. The run reflects the Borden gold mine in Ontario and the transformational 2025 acquisitions of the Porcupine and Kidd operations in Timmins; Discovery is guiding 260,000-300,000 oz gold production in 2026, weighted heavily to the second half.

headline: HOT CHILI DRILLS 62M AT 0.91% CUEQ FROM 20M DEPTH AT CHILE'S LA VERDE — HIGH-GRADE STARTER PIT CASE STRENGTHENS
snippet: Hot Chili Limited (ASX/TSXV: HCH) reported September 8 that hole DKP063 at the La Verde Cu-Au porphyry discovery in Chile's Atacama region returned 62m at 0.91% CuEq from 20m depth, within a broader 398m at 0.45% CuEq from surface — among the strongest near-surface results drilled at the project. Managing Director Easterday said comparable grades are now appearing across the deposit, strengthening the case for a high-grade starter pit at Costa Fuego, with 22 additional RC assays still pending.

headline: BRIEN LUNDIN: $40 TRILLION DEBT MAKES FED RATE HIKE CYCLE AN 'UNSUSTAINABLE BLUFF' — GOLD BULL STRUCTURALLY INTACT
snippet: Gold Newsletter editor Brien Lundin argues in a September 8 Money Metals Podcast interview that the Fed's tightening cycle faces a mathematical ceiling: with US federal debt above $40 trillion and debt-service costs already crowding out the budget, sustaining meaningfully higher rates risks a fiscal crisis before it tames inflation. Lundin sees the 'debasement trade' returning to precious metals as the structurally dominant force — making September's rate-hike anxiety a better entry signal than an exit for gold holders.

headline: INDIA'S GOLD IMPORTS NEARLY DOUBLE TO 40-45 TONNES IN JULY — DEMAND DEFIES MODI'S PLEA AND 15% CUSTOMS DUTY
snippet: India's gold imports surged from approximately 20 tonnes in June to an estimated 40-45 tonnes in July 2026 — even after Prime Minister Modi publicly urged citizens to forgo gold purchases for a year and the government hiked import customs duties from 6% to 15% in May. Q2 jewelry sales climbed roughly one-third year-over-year to $21 billion, confirming that physical demand from the world's second-largest gold buyer is absorbing higher prices rather than retreating, providing a structural floor that paper-market selloffs struggle to break.

headline: LUCA MINING OPENS CATORCE ZONE — 9.9M AT 5.39 G/T AUEQ IN FIRST SURFACE HOLE SINCE 2008 AT DURANGO MINE
snippet: Luca Mining Corp. (TSXV: LUCA) reported September 8 that the first surface hole at the under-explored Catorce Zone of the Tahuehueto gold-silver mine in Durango, Mexico returned 9.9m at 5.39 g/t AuEq (3.63 g/t Au, 70.14 g/t Ag, 1.69% Pb, 5.63% Zn) from 199.5m depth — including 1.0m at 27.56 g/t AuEq — the first drilling there since 2008. The Catorce Zone is interpreted as a southern extension of the high-grade Creston Vein system, roughly 250m from existing underground development, adding a potentially significant new resource vector at a producing mine.

headline: GREEN CANADA URANIUM (GCUC) HITS TSXV — ATHABASCA'S MARSHALL PROJECT DRILL-READY AS URANIUM HOLDS NEAR $90/LB
snippet: Green Canada Uranium Corp. (TSXV: GCUC) began trading on the TSX Venture Exchange around September 9, 2026, following the completion of its founding transaction with PTX Metals Equity Holding. The new vehicle holds 100% of the Marshall uranium project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — adjacent to IsoEnergy and Cameco assets — with diamond drilling expected to commence in September 2026, positioning the company to benefit from uranium spot near US$90/lb.
